clue.text: Legally organise condition accepted by buffalo hunter

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: William Cody, Buffalo Bill, was the famous American buffalo hunter
if introduces a condition, as in 'only if'

explanation.surface: A frontiersman agreeing to a stipulation and having it written into law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffalo hunter' reads as a description of any hunter, but it is the nickname of the American showman Buffalo Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To codify is to arrange laws or rules into a systematic written code.

clue.text: Tropical tree in California cut down — shame!

indicators.note: a word cut down is shortened, here losing everything after its first three letters

parts.note: the state name in full, before it is shortened
to shame someone is to abash them

explanation.surface: Someone in California laments a felled tree as a disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' looks like felling the tree but shortens CALIFORNIA to CAL, the usual abbreviation; then ABASH follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The calabash tree of tropical America bears large gourd-like fruits used as vessels.

clue.text: Don't avoid risky investments for wealthy old lady

parts.note: if you don't avoid something you do it
a wager is a bet, money put at risk on an uncertain outcome

explanation.surface: Advice to a rich elderly woman to embrace speculative finance.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding property or a title from her late husband, typically elderly and well-off.

clue.text: Company installing genuine article as safety device

indicators.note: a company installing something takes it inside, so the other pieces go within it

parts.note: a firm is a business company
real means genuine
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A firm fitting a real piece of kit to keep a building safe.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell or siren that warns occupants of smoke or flames is a key safety device.

clue.text: Work's bound to be available from this mail-order business

definitions.text: Work's bound to be available from this mail-order business

parts.words: Work's bound to be available from this mail-order business
parts.note: a work bound in covers is a book, and a mail-order firm selling such volumes by subscription is the business meant

explanation.surface: A firm promising that any published work will be in stock by post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work's bound' reads as 'the job is certain to be', but it is a literary work bound as a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: Subscription book businesses post members a regular selection of titles to buy.

clue.text: No place for closed minds?

parts.note: an institution with no entry requirements has no place for closed minds, and it is also no place at all, as teaching is by distance

explanation.surface: A remark that narrow-minded people would not fit in somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No place' works twice: the British distance-learning university admits anyone, and has no campus students attend.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's distance-learning institution, founded in 1969, admits students without formal qualifications.

clue.text: Poet giving king food

parts.note: K is the chess and cards abbreviation for king
eats is informal for food

explanation.surface: A poet handing provisions to a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: John Keats was the English Romantic who wrote 'Ode to a Nightingale'.

clue.text: Callas transformed a famous operatic scene

indicators.note: transformed means the letters are rearranged into a new form

parts.note: Maria Callas, the soprano, taken as written

explanation.surface: Maria Callas changing a celebrated moment in opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges CALLAS plus A; the 'scene' is a venue, not part of an opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan's great opera house is where much famous operatic action is staged.

clue.text: Unusually large cricket ball

definitions.meaning: a ... crop or harvest is exceptionally big
in cricket a short-pitched delivery that rears up at the batsman

explanation.surface: An outsized ball for the game of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a bowler's short ball that bounces up towards the batsman's head is called a bumper or bouncer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bumper means exceptionally plentiful, and in cricket it is a fast short-pitched delivery rising high.

clue.text: British annoy French novelist with dreadfully sham pub grub

parts.note: to anger is to annoy
George Sand was the pen name of the French novelist Aurore Dupin

indicators.note: dreadfully shows the following word is badly mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A complaint that a fake French writer is irritating British drinkers over their meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' rearranges SHAM to MASH. Bangers are British slang for sausages, served with mashed potato as a pub staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Sausages with mashed potato is a classic hearty dish served in British bars.

clue.text: Minor action he and she are in, not!

definitions.text: he and she are in, not!
definitions.note: the pronouns are printed here without initial capitals, which is what the closing 'not!' points at

parts.note: lower means minor or lesser in rank
a case is a legal action

explanation.surface: A small lawsuit with a man and woman involved, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minor action' looks like a small lawsuit and gives LOWER plus CASE; the rest says that small letters, not capitals, are how 'he' and 'she' are printed in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Small letters as opposed to capitals form this style, in which ordinary pronouns appear.

clue.text: Like American uncle in eastern state

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as good as new'
Uncle Sam personifies the United States

explanation.surface: A relative from America visiting an eastern region, in a manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Assam is a state in north-east India, famous for its tea.

clue.text: Important report of what happened initially

parts.note: big means important, as in a big decision
a report is a loud bang, as of a gun

explanation.surface: A significant account of the first events in some story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like an account but is the noise of an explosion; 'initially' refers to the origin of the universe.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmologists hold that the universe began with a primordial explosion, the event at the very start.

clue.text: Eclipse seen from raised platform

definitions.meaning: to outshine someone, drawing attention from them
..., at the back of a raked theatre stage that rises away from the audience

explanation.surface: An eclipse watched from a high viewing stand.
explanation.walkthrough: Old theatre stages sloped upward away from the audience, so the rear part was literally raised.
explanation.definitionFit: To outshine a fellow actor by standing at the back; and positioned at the rear of a stage.

clue.text: As initially taken from republic

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'As initially taken from republic (5)': SYRIA is ASSYRIA without its opening AS, but no clue word gives ASSYRIA, so a word of the clue appears to be missing and no search found the full text

clue.text: Coats, for example, put on by painter at home

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
in means at home
to wear clothes is to have them put on

explanation.surface: An artist at home slipping on coats and similar garments.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for a member of the Royal Academy, Britain's arts body, so a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Raincoats, macs and cagoules are examples of clothing for wet weather.

clue.text: Flower of one colour, otherwise variegated

indicators.note: variegated means patterned in different colours, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A bloom in a single shade, unless it is the mottled kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variegated' rearranges OTHERWISE; the clue sets a single colour against mottled markings.
explanation.definitionFit: The bloom is a pale bloom of a single hue, emblem of Yorkshire and the House of York.

clue.text: Gemstone they set unusually, in American way

indicators.note: a stone set in a ring is placed inside it, so one piece goes within the others
in completes the setting instruction, showing where the shuffled word goes

parts.note: St, street, is a way

indicators.note: unusually shows the word they appears in an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: A jeweller's people mounting a gem in an odd, American fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' suggests mounting a gem, which fits the surface, but with 'in' it tells the solver to place the jumbled word inside the others.
explanation.definitionFit: The violet variety of quartz is cut and polished as a jewel.

clue.text: A river barrier's disposal producing water

parts.note: a dam is a barrier across a river
a sale is a disposal of goods

explanation.surface: Getting rid of a weir produces a flood.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe moves: 'barrier's' is a possessive in the clue, but the answer splits after the M, a humorous name from the Bible's first man.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a humorous name for plain drinking water, the only drink of the first man.

clue.text: Spirited hurling

definitions.meaning: lively and stylish, full of dash
throwing violently, as in smashing something down

explanation.surface: A lively performance in the Irish stick game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hurling' suggests the Irish field sport, but here it means flinging.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing describes a lively, stylish person; to dash something is to throw it hard.

clue.text: Man attached to one daughter, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
IOM is the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A man linked to a single daughter, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the Isle of Man, the island between Britain and Ireland, abbreviated IOM.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed expression whose sense differs from its literal words.

clue.text: Entering with double gin, confused about round

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other
confused shows the doubled letters are jumbled
double means the word gin is taken twice

parts.note: O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone arriving after two gins, muddled about whose round it is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' gives GINGIN, 'confused' turns it to INGING, and 'about' wraps that round O between the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingoing means coming in or going in, as an ingoing tenant moves into a property.

clue.text: Some in parish are dogmatically divided

indicators.note: Some in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A congregation split by doctrinal argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divided' looks like a split congregation, but here it means apportioned, as when something is divided among people.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shared is split out among several people.

clue.text: Thriftily manage as a partner

definitions.meaning: to use resources carefully and economically
a married man is his wife's partner

explanation.surface: Advice to handle money carefully as a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband resources is to use them sparingly; a husband is a man's role in a marriage.

clue.text: A brilliant instrument, or a dull one

parts.note: mat, or matt, means dull, without shine
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A violin could be dazzling or lacklustre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Amati family of Cremona made fine violins; 'brilliant' and 'dull' look like opposite verdicts on one violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Violins by the Amati family of 16th and 17th century Cremona are prized concert instruments.

clue.text: Conjuror's skill meaning little to audience

indicators.note: to an audience the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: slight means small or meaning little

explanation.surface: A magician's craft counts for little with the people watching.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'audience' looks like the conjuror's spectators, but it signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight of hand is the dexterity a magician uses to deceive onlookers.

clue.text: Indian dish Kipling, for example, announced

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so a word is heard

parts.note: Rudyard Kipling was a writer

explanation.surface: An Indian dish declared by Kipling, who wrote about India.
explanation.walkthrough: The homophone works in a non-rhotic British accent where the final R of the word for an author is not sounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Raita is a yogurt side dish with cucumber or mint served in Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Expert is right to make decisions

definitions.meaning: a recognised specialist on a subject
the power or entitlement to give orders

explanation.surface: A specialist has the power to decide.
explanation.definitionFit: An authority is an acknowledged expert; it is also the power to command or decide.

clue.text: Highly dangerous combat -involving boxers, maybe

parts.note: aerial combat between fighter planes high up, or a fight between dogs, of which boxers are a breed

explanation.surface: A risky bout between prize fighters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxers' suggests pugilists but is the dog breed; 'Highly' points at air combat.
explanation.definitionFit: Close combat between fighter aircraft shares its name with a scrap between hounds.

clue.text: Make heavier women's plus fours?

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
four plus four makes eight

explanation.surface: A suggestion that women's baggy golfing trousers add bulk.
explanation.walkthrough: Plus fours are baggy knee-length trousers once worn for golf; here they are read as the sum 4 + 4.
explanation.definitionFit: To weight something is to add ballast or load to it.
